title: Ansel and the Interior
premise: Cyrus Lockridge, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost the ability to taste years ago, drifts through a life of borrowed opinions until a radio plays an unfinished song their late mother wrote and never recorded — and Cyrus is pulled into its melody, reliving fragments of the family history that song was meant to hold. Inside the song's unfinished middle, Cyrus discovers what really happened the night their brother Ansel left home, a truth the family buried to protect itself, and learns Ansel is dying in a town no one thought to look for him. To finish the song — and reach Ansel before it's too late — Cyrus must choose between the family's careful silence and a justice the law never delivered. The book ends with Cyrus performing the completed song at Ansel's bedside, trading their career's last shred of detachment for the taste of salt on their own lips.
about_author: Juniper Yarrow is the pen name of a former line cook turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unpublished recordings in a university basement. This is their second novel, written mostly in diner booths after closing time.

chapters.title: A Tenant in His Own Mouth
chapters.summary: Cyrus reviews a tasting menu they cannot taste, describing texture and reputation while feeling nothing, then goes home to a spotless apartment that feels like a hotel. A phone call from their sister Wren about Mother's estate goes unanswered. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: numb competence masking grief.

chapters.title: Static Between Stations
chapters.summary: Driving to settle the estate, Cyrus hears a folk song on a rural station — unmistakably their mother's melody, with lyrics she only ever hummed. They pull over, shaking, and trace the signal to a one-room community radio run by an old DJ named Hollis. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: wonder cracking open routine.

chapters.title: What the Song Remembers
chapters.summary: Hollis explains the tape arrived unsigned years ago; when Cyrus touches it, they are pulled inside the music into a kitchen memory from 1994 — Mother playing, young Ansel listening at the door. The song ends mid-phrase, and Cyrus wakes with flour on their hands. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: awe edged with dread.

chapters.title: The Arrangement
chapters.summary: At the family house, Cyrus confronts Wren and their father Gerald, who insist Ansel chose to leave after 'the trouble' and forbid digging it up. Flashback within the song shows the family agreeing on a story. POV: alternating Cyrus and Wren. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Verse Two
chapters.summary: Drawn back into the song, Cyrus witnesses the night Ansel took blame for something Gerald did — a hit-and-run covered up by money and silence. Ansel was seventeen. Cyrus, who always believed Ansel abandoned them, reels. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal reordering every childhood memory.

chapters.title: Hollis's Ledger
chapters.summary: Hollis reveals he knew Ansel — the tape came from him, mailed from a town called Marrow Bend — and gives Cyrus a box of unsent letters. Reading them, Cyrus tastes for the first time in years: bitter coffee, real and overwhelming. POV: alternating Cyrus and letters. Emotional beat: grief as the return of sensation.

chapters.title: Marrow Bend
chapters.summary: Cyrus drives to find Ansel working a diner kitchen, ill and unrepentant about his exile. He refuses forgiveness but asks one thing: finish the song, because Mother wrote it for him and it stops where his life did. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: pride worn thin enough to see through.

chapters.title: The Bridge No One Wrote
chapters.summary: Wren arrives, having found Gerald's confession in the estate papers, torn between protecting her father and her brother. The siblings argue in the diner parking lot until Wren admits she always suspected. Together they draft the song's missing bridge. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: duty bending toward love.

chapters.title: Gerald at the Door
chapters.summary: Gerald tracks them down, demanding they bury it again; Cyrus instead makes him listen to the tape in the car, forcing him to hear Ansel's voice singing his own sacrifice. Gerald weeps but will not confess publicly — so Cyrus decides the justice owed isn't legal but sung. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the climax of choice over comfort.

chapters.title: The Whole Song, Sung
chapters.summary: In Ansel's hospital room, Cyrus and Wren perform the finished song as Hollis records it; Ansel sings the final verse himself and dies two days later, at peace. The recording airs on Hollis's small station, reaching more ears than any review ever did. Cyrus eats a peach and tastes everything. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: belonging earned through truth.
